sources.title: Compaction - Claude Platform Docs
sources.summary: Anthropic's server-side compaction automatically summarizes older conversation content when input tokens cross a threshold, emitting a compaction block that replaces prior history. Anthropic now recommends it over client-side SDK compaction.
key_facts: compact_20260112 edit enabled via context_management.edits; beta header anthropic-beta: compact-2026-01-12
Default trigger 150,000 input tokens; minimum allowed trigger value 50,000 tokens
pause_after_compaction flag lets client adjust messages after summary; custom instructions fully replace default summarization prompt
Supported models: Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos; beta on API, Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry
Compaction pass billed separately: usage.iterations shows e.g. 180,000 input tokens for compaction; top-level usage excludes it
Anthropic: 'Server-side compaction is the recommended strategy'; client-side SDK compaction deprecated
ZDR-eligible; count_tokens returns original_input_tokens vs post-compaction input_tokens
Recommends cache_control breakpoint on system prompt so only the summary is rewritten to cache after compaction

sources.title: Context editing - Claude Platform Docs
sources.summary: Server-side context editing lets developers declaratively clear old tool results and thinking blocks before the prompt reaches Claude, while the client keeps full history. Absorbs a common hand-rolled pruning pattern.
key_facts: clear_tool_uses_20250919: default trigger 100,000 input tokens, keep 3 most recent tool uses; exclude_tools and clear_tool_inputs options
clear_at_least parameter sets minimum tokens to clear so cache-write cost is justified
clear_thinking_20251015 keeps N recent thinking turns; Opus 4.5+ and Sonnet 4.6+ keep all prior thinking by default
Beta header anthropic-beta: context-management-2025-06-27; available on all supported Claude models
Response returns applied_edits with cleared_tool_uses and cleared_input_tokens (e.g. 50,000 tokens cleared)
Tool result clearing invalidates cached prefixes; docs flag the tension between editing and prompt caching
Designed to pair with memory tool so Claude saves facts before tool results are cleared

sources.title: Memory tool - Claude Platform Docs
sources.summary: Anthropic's memory tool lets Claude treat memory as local files it reads and writes under a /memories directory, with the developer owning storage. Docs position it as the complement to compaction for long-running agents.
key_facts: memory_20250818 tool released September 29, 2025 (per search summary); Claude reads/writes memory as files
Docs: use compaction and memory together — compaction keeps active context small, memory preserves what must survive summarization
Storage is client-side: the developer implements file backend, so the vendor does not host the memory store

sources.title: Claude Memory Tool in Practice: The Complete Guide to Giving Your Agent Cross-Session Memory
sources.summary: Third-party implementation guide for Anthropic's memory tool, summarizing Anthropic's stated internal results and the recommended memory-plus-context-editing pattern.
key_facts: Cites Anthropic using memory tool plus context editing internally in Claude Code with 29-39% performance improvement reported
Guide frames memory as developer-hosted files, positioning the tool as a protocol rather than a hosted memory service

sources.title: Feature: Anthropic Context Editing API Integration — Server-Side, Cache-Friendly Tool/Thinking Cleanup (hermes-agent #526)
sources.summary: Open-source agent framework issue requesting native integration of Anthropic's server-side context editing, a signal that vendor-side pruning is being adopted downstream instead of framework-level heuristics.
key_facts: Issue frames Anthropic context editing as 'server-side, cache-friendly tool/thinking cleanup' worth integrating into hermes-agent
Signal: OSS harnesses prefer delegating pruning to the vendor API rather than maintaining client-side logic

sources.title: Claude pricing in 2026: every plan, API rate, and what it actually costs
sources.summary: Pricing roundup showing Anthropic folded 1M-token context into standard per-token pricing for 4.6+ models and that prompt-cache reads are discounted 90%, compressing the economic case for external context-shrinking tools.
key_facts: Claude Opus 4.6: $5.00 per million input tokens, $25.00 per million output tokens
Claude Sonnet 4.6: $3.00 input / $15.00 output; 1M context at standard pricing, no long-context premium
A 900k-token request billed at the same per-token rate as a 9k-token request
Prompt cache reads cost 90% less; Sonnet 4.6 cached read $0.30/MTok vs $3.00
Article contrasts Claude 90% caching discount with OpenAI 50% cached-input discount

sources.title: Claude 1M Context GA: Practical Rollout Guide
sources.summary: Rollout guide marking the date Anthropic moved 1M-token context from beta to general availability on its 4.6 models.
key_facts: Anthropic announced 1M context GA for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on March 13, 2026
As of March 14, 2026 the guide describes 1M context as production-ready for 4.6 long-context workloads

sources.title: Compaction | OpenAI API
sources.summary: OpenAI's Responses API offers automatic server-side compaction via context_management.compact_threshold plus an explicit /responses/compact endpoint; compacted state is an encrypted item carried forward into the next turn.
key_facts: Server-side compaction released February 11, 2026 via the Responses API (per search summary)
Set context_management with compact_threshold; compaction runs automatically when rendered tokens cross threshold, no separate call
Compaction item is encrypted and 'carries forward key prior state and reasoning into the next run using fewer tokens'
ZDR-friendly when store=false on Responses create requests
With previous_response_id chaining pass only the new user message; 'do not manually prune'
Stateless chaining may drop items before the latest compaction item to cut request size and tail latency
/responses/compact output is 'the canonical next context window'; examples reference gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5.6
Docs list no pricing or explicit token accounting for the compaction pass

sources.title: Conversation state | OpenAI API
sources.summary: OpenAI's conversation-state guide documents server-held state via previous_response_id chaining and the Conversations API, so developers need not ship full history each turn.
key_facts: previous_response_id chaining: send only the new user message each turn; server reconstructs prior context
Server-side state plus compaction together absorb the 'history store + summarizer' layer many startups sold in 2024-2025

sources.title: [Feature Request] Support OpenAI server-side compaction (context_management) in @ai-sdk/openai (vercel/ai #12486)
sources.summary: Feature request for the Vercel AI SDK to surface OpenAI's server-side compaction, showing that vendor-native compaction outpaces framework support and that developers want it exposed rather than reimplemented.
key_facts: Request asks @ai-sdk/openai to pass through OpenAI context_management compaction settings
Signal: middleware/framework layers must expose vendor compaction or risk being bypassed

sources.title: Azure OpenAI Response API: Input Token Counting with previous_response_id and Support for Server-Side Context Compaction
sources.summary: Azure customer question about how input tokens are counted under previous_response_id chaining and whether server-side compaction is available on Azure, illustrating cost-observability confusion created by server-held state.
key_facts: Customers cannot easily see how many input tokens server-side state contributes per turn under previous_response_id
Azure availability of OpenAI server-side compaction lags the first-party API, per the question

sources.title: Compaction API (/responses/compact) - TrueFoundry Docs
sources.summary: An AI-gateway vendor documents passthrough support for OpenAI's /responses/compact, showing compaction becoming a gateway checkbox feature rather than a differentiated product.
key_facts: TrueFoundry AI Gateway exposes OpenAI /responses/compact through its proxy
Signal: gateways absorb compaction as a pass-through feature, narrowing standalone compaction products

sources.title: Compact a Response with Previous Response ID - OpenAI Developer Community
sources.summary: Developer forum threads asking how /responses/compact interacts with previous_response_id and the Conversations API, showing that vendor compaction shipped with rough edges around state-chaining modes.
key_facts: Companion thread 1378730 asks the same question for the Conversations API
Pain point: three state modes (stateless input array, previous_response_id, Conversations) have different compaction rules

sources.title: Agent memory - OpenAI Agents SDK (sandbox memory)
sources.summary: OpenAI's Agents SDK added sandbox memory that distills lessons from prior runs into workspace markdown files, separate from Session message history, replicating the file-based memory pattern popularized by coding agents.
key_facts: Default layout: memories/memory_summary.md injected at run start, memories/MEMORY.md keyword index, raw_memories/, rollout_summaries/, sessions/*.jsonl
Two-phase pipeline: conversation extraction model then consolidation agent writes MEMORY.md and memory_summary.md
MemoryGenerateConfig.max_raw_memories_for_consolidation defaults to 256; extra_prompt for domain guidance
Recency-based forgetting removes older raw memories past the configured limit
Memory reads require Shell() capability; live updates require Filesystem(); sandbox agents are in beta
Stated goal: reduce agent cost, user cost and context cost for future runs

sources.title: Sessions - OpenAI Agents SDK
sources.summary: Agents SDK Sessions persist conversation history keyed by session_id with SQLite, SQLAlchemy, Redis and encrypted backends, making short-term memory a built-in SDK primitive.
key_facts: SQLiteSession defaults to in-memory DB lost at process end; pass a file path for persistence
Backends listed: SQLite, SQLAlchemy, Redis, encrypted sessions; same session_id means the agent remembers
Session history is injected automatically into runs, making memory 'invisible infrastructure'

sources.title: OpenAI Agents SDK Sandboxes Harness and Memory — AgentPatterns.ai
sources.summary: Directory entry summarizing the April 2026 Agents SDK update that bundled a model-native harness, sandbox execution and configurable memory into OpenAI's own agent stack.
key_facts: OpenAI Agents SDK update dated 2026-04-15 consolidates three primitives: model-native harness, native sandbox execution, configurable memory
Two memory systems: Session (SQLAlchemy, SQLite, Redis, encrypted) and sandbox memory (filesystem-distilled lessons across runs)

sources.title: OpenAI Agents Forget Everything Between Runs. Here's the Fix.
sources.summary: A memory-layer startup publishes a how-to positioning its product as the persistent-memory fix for the OpenAI Agents SDK two days after OpenAI's own memory update, illustrating the 'plug the vendor gap' go-to-market.
key_facts: Published April 17, 2026, two days after the 2026-04-15 Agents SDK memory update
GTM pattern: vendor-specific integration tutorials targeting developers of the incumbent SDK

sources.title: Vertex AI Memory Bank in public preview
sources.summary: Google launched Memory Bank, a managed long-term memory service that asynchronously extracts, consolidates and retrieves user memories from Agent Engine Sessions using Gemini, with ADK integration and API access for LangGraph and CrewAI.
key_facts: Announced July 8, 2025 as public preview inside Vertex AI Agent Engine
Uses Gemini to extract key facts and preferences asynchronously from Agent Engine Sessions conversation history
Consolidates new memories with existing ones and resolves contradictions; retrieval by all-facts or embedding similarity search
Out-of-the-box ADK integration; LangGraph and CrewAI supported via API
Grounded in Google Research method accepted at ACL 2025 (arxiv 2503.08026)
Free tier via express mode with a Gmail API key; $300 credit for new Google Cloud customers

sources.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform pricing | Google Cloud
sources.summary: Google's pricing page sets usage-based rates for Agent Engine Sessions and Memory Bank, turning managed agent memory into a metered cloud line item.
key_facts: Sessions and Memory Bank billing began February 11, 2026
Sessions and Memory Bank: $0.25 per 1,000 events or memories
Agent Engine runtime: $0.0864 per vCPU-hour and $0.0090 per GB-hour

sources.title: Google Vertex AI Pricing: Complete Enterprise Guide (2026)
sources.summary: Enterprise pricing guide noting Gemini context caching on Vertex AI discounts cached tokens by 90%, a direct lever against the cost of very long contexts.
key_facts: Vertex AI context caching priced at a 90% discount versus standard input pricing
Positions caching as the main tool for managing long context windows efficiently

sources.title: Vertex AI Agent Builder: 2026 guide to Google's enterprise AI agent platform
sources.summary: Overview of Google's agent stack where ADK is the model-agnostic code framework and Agent Engine is the managed runtime owning sessions, memory, autoscaling and long-running execution.
key_facts: ADK is model-agnostic: usable with Gemini, Claude or open models; deploys to any container or Kubernetes
Agent Engine managed runtime handles autoscaling, sub-second cold starts, session management and long-running execution

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing: 12 Components Breakdown
sources.summary: Component-level breakdown of AgentCore pricing, including short-term event pricing and the two long-term memory storage tiers that price Amazon's managed agent memory.
key_facts: AgentCore reached general availability on October 13, 2025
Short-term memory: $0.25 per 1,000 new events (one event per CreateEvent call)
Long-term memory built-in automatic extraction: $0.75 per 1,000 records/month; self-managed or override strategy: $0.25 per 1,000 records/month
Long-term memory retrieval: $0.50 per 1,000 retrievals, charged regardless of storage strategy
Built-in extraction bundles model inference into the per-record rate, a 67% storage cost gap vs self-managed
Short-term event expiration cannot be set below 7 days

sources.title: Add memory to your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent
sources.summary: AWS developer guide for AgentCore Memory, which splits session-scoped short-term memory from cross-session long-term memory populated by extraction strategies.
key_facts: Short-term memory keeps coherence within a single session; long-term memory persists preferences across days, weeks or months
Pay-per-use with no upfront costs or minimum commitments

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing (2026): What Actually Drives the Bill
sources.summary: 2026 cost analysis finding that runtime duration and long-term memory dominate AgentCore bills and flagging retention rules that lock in memory storage costs.
key_facts: As of June 2026 in us-east-1, runtime duration and long-term Memory are the dominant cost lines for production agents
Short-term events cannot expire in under 7 days and 30/90-day retention cannot be force-expired

sources.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Version 1.0
sources.summary: Microsoft shipped Agent Framework 1.0, merging Semantic Kernel and AutoGen, with pluggable context providers for memory and first-party connectors to Foundry Memory, Mem0, Redis and Neo4j.
key_facts: Released April 3, 2026 as a single open-source SDK unifying Semantic Kernel and AutoGen
Agent Memory and Context Providers are pluggable: conversational history, key-value state, vector-based retrieval
Memory backends: Memory in Foundry Agent Service, Mem0, Redis, Neo4j, custom stores
Connectors for Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, Ollama; A2A and MCP support
Foundry integration includes managed tools, memory services, OpenTelemetry observability and evaluation dashboards
Roadmap: graduate preview features, expand connectors and skills, deepen Foundry integration; 'Version 1.0 is a beginning, not a destination'
Mem0 ships as an official provider package (agent-framework-mem0), validating startup memory layers inside incumbent frameworks

.github/copilot-instructions.md 'loads into every Copilot Chat conversation automatically' but is 'static text' maintained manually with 'no concept of time'
Author: 'Every AI coding assistant on the market has the same constraint — Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf'
Pain cited: architectural decisions, team conventions and debugging investigations must be re-established each session

sources.title: Cursor vs Windsurf vs GitHub Copilot in 2026: Which AI Code Editor Actually Wins?
sources.summary: 2026 IDE comparison describing Windsurf's persistent Memories and Cascade context tracking versus Cursor's codebase indexing and Copilot's narrower project-wide capabilities.
key_facts: Windsurf Memories persist context across conversations; Cascade tracks edits, commands, clipboard and terminal output to infer intent
Article claims Copilot lacks an advanced project-wide assistant comparable to Cursor Agent Mode or Windsurf Cascade
Cursor relies on codebase indexing; article says Windsurf Memories persist across sessions more effectively

Cascade Memories is a persistent session memory that remembers past actions across longer coding sessions
